finding: replace_text retry test patches time.sleep but never asserts the pause, so the 50 ms wait between swaps is unproven
why: Mutation probe: replacing `time.sleep(pause)` with `pass` in outside_writes.py:871 (and changing the default `tries: int = 20` to 3) leaves all 96 tests green, yet D-30's fix for a scanner-held file rests on retries being spaced 50 ms apart up to 20 times; instant retries would hit the same held file.
fix: Keep the sleep mock and assert it was called `tries-1` times with 0.05 (e.g. `sleep.assert_has_calls([mock.call(0.05)] * 2)`); add one assertion that the default gives up after 20 replace calls.
evidence:
with mock.patch("outside_writes.os.replace", held_twice), mock.patch("outside_writes.time.sleep"):
        replace_text(target, "new")
    assert target.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "new" and len(calls) == 3

finding: No test covers proof names and the proof heading for a created ticket whose folder did not move; reverting them to the work id goes unnoticed
why: Mutation probe: changing `plan.mark_id` to `plan.work_id` in `_stage` (publish_bug_mode.py:530) or in the `**Proof for ...**` line (publish_bug_mode.py:704) leaves every test green, because the folder-move-later test has no proof and every proof test either moves the folder (work id becomes the key) or uses an existing ticket (mark id equals work id). D-29(b) says a created ticket "keys its markers and proof names on its key from the first run, so a folder move on a later run changes neither".
fix: Extend the later-move test (or add one) with `proof=` on a first run using `resolve=lambda key: None`, then assert the attached file name starts with `PROJ-1-p-1-proof-` and the comment heading reads `Proof for PROJ-1`, and that the re-run after the move uploads nothing new.

criterion: error and rollback paths / partial-failure handling (re-run after a write that took effect but was not listed)
finding: A re-run is refused before any write when the in-review move already took effect but is not listed, or the ticket was put in review by hand, whenever `jira.transitions.in-review` is a transition id or name
why: The new skip at line 430 covers only a listed move; otherwise `_in_review_target` runs, the workflow no longer offers the transition, and its fallback (`_in_state(state, ("status", value))`, line 469) compares the status name to the configured transition id or name, which never match, so the step's own read-back (`_move_to_in_review` with read_first) is never reached and BUG-MODE.md:32's 'unless the ticket is already in that state' does not hold.
fix: When no transition matches, read the ticket state and accept it when it equals the `to` status of the configured transition as last seen, or defer the match to `_move_to_in_review`'s read-back; at minimum treat a ticket whose status has no outgoing match as already moved only after checking the state against a configured status name, and document that the value must be the status name.
evidence: Probe with the suite's own JIRA config (`transitions: {in-review: "31"}`) and StubJiraInReview, existing ticket PROJ-9: run 1 with `append_outside_write` raising PermissionError for `in-review:` -> `FAILED: [Errno 13] Access is denied; the writes reported above stay on the tracker` and status `In Review`; run 2 (nothing failing) -> code 1 `REFUSED: PROJ-9 offers no transition matching the in-review value `31`; it offers: Back to dev (21); nothing was written`. Same refusal for a ticket already `In Review` by hand. Code: `if in_review and target_key and (description or not listed(source, f"in-review: {target_key}")):` then `target = _in_review_target(run, target_key, str(value))`.

criterion: boundary values / idempotency of re-runs (same ticket, another key spelling)
finding: `later` compares key strings, so the recorded ticket given again in another spelling (`#5` for `5`) is treated as a different ticket and a second evidence comment is posted on the same issue
why: The GitHub adapter accepts `123`, `#123` and `owner/repo#123` for one issue (`_number`, adapters/tracker/github-issues/api.py:153-159), but `plan.given != plan.recorded` adds the `-{key}` suffix, the marker changes from `... evidence` to `... evidence-5`, the listed entry and the read-back no longer match, and the comment is written again; before this delta the unchanged marker was listed and the step skipped (Jira lower-case keys likely hit the same path; unverified whether Jira resolves `proj-2`).
fix: Normalise both keys before comparing (resolve the given key through `tracker_get` and compare the canonical key/number the tracker returns), and use the canonical key in the `ticket:` entry and the suffix.
evidence: Probe with a GitHub stub that normalises `#5` like `_number`: run 1 on Ticket key `5` posts the evidence; run 2 with `key="#5"` -> `STEP: ticket — #5 listed in Outside writes`, `STEP: evidence — comment posted`; issue 5 has 2 comments; Outside writes: `- evidence: afk-evidence bug-export-drops-row evidence` / `- ticket: #5` / `- evidence: afk-evidence bug-export-drops-row evidence-5`. Code: `later = bool(plan.given and plan.recorded and plan.given != plan.recorded)`.

finding: Proof staging now runs after the spec-folder move, so a proof file kept in the spec folder is gone when it is copied, and the run fails after the create and the evidence comment
why: The delta moved `_stage(plan)` from before `_execute` (where copies were taken while every preflight-checked path still existed) to after `_move`, which renames the folder holding the diagnosis; a re-run with the same --proof path is then refused at preflight ('no such proof file').
fix: Stage the proof copies before the first write (before `_steps` runs `_create`/`_move`), keeping only the name computation late, or re-map proof paths under the moved folder.
evidence: Probe (StubJira, proof at docs/bug-export-drops-row/shot.png beside DIAGNOSIS.md, create run): lines 'STEP: ticket — spec folder moved to ...\docs\PROJ-1', 'STEP: evidence — comment posted', "FAILED: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '...\docs\bug-export-drops-row\shot.png'; the writes reported above stay on the tracker; no write followed it". Code: `_move(run, plan, resolve)` at :576 precedes `if plan.proof:\n        _stage(plan)` at :589-590; removed lines `-        staged = _stage(plan)\n-        key_now, link = _execute(run, plan, resolve, staged)`.

finding: "Every option" command-line test never passes --fix-version; dropping it in main() survives
why: Mutation probe: replacing `fix_version=args.fix_version,` with `fix_version=None,` in `main()` leaves all tests green, because both command-line tests run against the GitHub config, where fix version is refused, and the slice's commit message claims every option is tested.
fix: Add a Jira-config command-line case (or a dry run) with `--fix-version 1.5` and assert the plan line or the `tracker_edit` payload carries `1.5`.

finding: Possible conditional test logic: a loop of four argparse refusals plus a dry run and a consent refusal in one test body
why: When one argv in the loop stops raising SystemExit, the failure does not say which one, and the test mixes three behaviours (dry run, missing consent, argparse refusals), which makes it an eager test.
fix: Move the argv refusals into a `@pytest.mark.parametrize` test and split the dry run and consent cases into separate tests.
evidence:
for argv in (["--type", "bug"], ["--diagnosis", str(path), "--description", str(path)],
                 ["--diagnosis", str(path), "--dry-run", "--yes"], ["--diagnosis", str(path), "--proof", "P-1"]):
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
            mode.main(argv)

finding: Write-order table drifts from the code: the suffix is a lowercased slug, not `-{key}`, and the proof row still names files `{work id}-...` while the code now uses the created ticket's key
why: An agent reading the table to find an earlier write or an uploaded file looks for the wrong marker/name (D-29 (b) says proof names are keyed on the created key).
fix: Say the suffix is `-{key, lowercased}` and change the proof row to `{work id, or the key of a ticket this mode created}-{kind}-proof-{file name}`.
evidence: BUG-MODE.md:44 'a later different key adds `-{key}` to the step'; :45 'files named `{work id}-{kind}-proof-{file name}`'; code :579 `suffix = f"-{_slug(plan.key)}"` with `_slug` = `text.lower()`; :530 `base = f"{plan.mark_id}-{kind_name.lower()}-proof-..."`; test asserts 'evidence-proj-3'.

finding: A description file whose name has a space or other non-id character is now refused, because the raw file stem joins the work id
why: The new work id `{folder}-{stem}` is checked against SAFE_ID before any write, so a file name the user chose (not a work id) blocks the run with a message about the work id, a case the folder-only id never hit.
fix: Slug the stem (as `_slug` does for keys) before joining it into the work id, or refuse with a message naming the file name.
evidence: `work_id = f"{source.resolve().parent.name}-{source.stem}"`; probe with docs/adhoc/'my note.md': ['REFUSED: work id `adhoc-my note` must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ to be searchable; nothing was written']

finding: replace_text with tries<=0 never swaps, returns as if it wrote, and leaves its temporary file behind
why: The new public `tries` parameter has no lower bound; the loop body never runs so neither `return` nor `raise` fires and the cleanup in `except` is skipped.
fix: Clamp `tries` to at least 1 (or raise ValueError on tries < 1).
evidence: `for left in range(tries - 1, -1, -1):`; probe `replace_text(target, 'new', tries=0)` -> files ['.D.md.b934z8kb', 'D.md'], content 'old', no exception.
